contexts.text: Thou hatest the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate () = that from their truths they know and thence do not will their works to be meritorious, because this is contrary to the merit and justice of the Lord. That the works of the Nicolaitans are meritorious works, it has been given to know from revelation.
So hast thou... them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which I hate () = that there are among them also those who make works meritorious. (Explained.)
That the Christian Church has been so vexed and torn from its infancy, is evident from... Nicholas, from whom the Nicolaitans were named, who are mentioned in ; ; and also by Cerinthus.
The Nicolaitans = those who separate good from truth, or charity from faith... Explained. AE 142.
That those who separate charity from faith are called Nicolaitans, is chiefly from the sound of that word in Heaven; for its sound is from truth or faith, and not from good or charity.
